title: Synthesis and Surgery: Prompt Lab Portfolio for Code Gen + Refactor Evals
content:
Purpose:
This working catalog collects a compact, pragmatic prompt suite and an accompanying regression report template used when onboarding new model candidates for code generation and automated refactoring tasks. Focus areas: compile-first correctness, unit-test alignment, and style/constraint fidelity. The goal is to provide quick signal for: (1) whether a candidate can produce runnable patches, (2) whether refactors preserve behavior, and (3) whether generated code meets style constraints enforced by our linters and internal guidelines.

Scope and intended use:
- Primary: automated CI-style gating for model candidates when added to the model catalog.
- Secondary: prompt engineering playground for evaluating prompt variants, few-shot examples, and system messages for safety and intent preservation.
- Not in scope: large-scale data collection for training; this is an eval/guard-rail artifact.

Prompt taxonomy (high level):
1) Synthesis (generate new implementation) — prompts that ask for fully implemented functions/modules with minimal scaffolding. Evaluation: compiles + unit tests pass.
2) Surgery (targeted refactor/patch) — prompts that give a failing test or a code smell and ask for a specific patch. Evaluation: preserves or restores behavior, compiles, small diff size.
3) Test-authoring (unit test generation) — prompts that ask the model to write focused unit tests for a given function. Evaluation: tests run deterministically and surface realistic edge cases.
4) Style-conformance (lint and formatting constraints) — prompts that require stylistic constraints (naming, line length, docstrings). Evaluation: linter scores and automated style gating.

Core evaluation metrics (automated):
- compile_rate: percent of outputs that compile under target toolchain (language-specific toolchain dockerized).
- test_pass_rate: percent of generated tests that pass when run against reference implementations (or percent of generated patches that cause tests to pass).
- behavior_preservation: for refactors, proportion of inputs where outputs match golden behavior within tolerance (diff-based and test-based).
- style_violation_rate: fraction of outputs flagged by our style linter (we map to per-rule counts).
- patch_size_median: median lines changed for surgical fixes (smaller is better, all else equal).
- time_to_compile_median: wall time in CI for compile (used to detect pathological answers with huge dependencies).
- token_efficiency: tokens produced per successful compile/pass (cost proxy).

Experimental harness overview:
- Each prompt is executed against N seeds (N=10 default) with temperature sweep: [0.0, 0.2, 0.6]. Deterministic run is temperature=0.0.
- Outputs are wrapped into the target repo sandbox and run in ephemeral containers matching our standard LTS images.
- Linters: clang-tidy/pyflakes/gofmt/eslint run with configured rule sets.
- Tests: harness executes pytest/junit/go test based on language. Timeouts: 30s per compile, 10s per test.
- Regression detection: we compare model candidate results against a baseline model (latest production candidate) and flag any drop > 5% in compile_rate or > 10% relative regression in test_pass_rate for manual review.

Prompt templates and representative examples (kept short to emphasize different evaluation axes):
A) Synthesis: implement algorithm with constraints
Prompt: "Implement a function `remove_duplicates` in Python that de-duplicates a list in-place with O(1) additional memory. Include a docstring and two unit tests using pytest."
Expected checks: compiles, passes tests, uses in-place operations (heuristic: no creation of new list objects in top-level flow), docstring present, line length < 100.

B) Surgery: small targeted bugfix
Prompt: "Given the following JavaScript function and failing test (shown below), produce a minimal patch that fixes the bug without changing the public API. Return a unified patch (git diff -U3). Failing test: assertion that `flatten([1,[2,3]])` returns `[1,2,3]`. Function: (provided)."
Expected checks: patch applies cleanly, tests pass, patch_size <= 20 lines, behavior preserved for other existing tests.

C) Test-authoring: edge case discovery
Prompt: "Write three focused pytest unit tests for a function `serialize_user(user)` that converts a nested dict to JSON string, paying attention to datetime serialization and missing fields. Use parametrized tests."
Expected checks: tests run, at least one test targets datetime edge case, tests are deterministic.

D) Style-conformance: naming and typing
Prompt: "Refactor this Go function to follow our style guide: exported functions must have comments, error return values should be named `err`, and lines should not exceed 100 chars. Keep behavior identical."
Expected checks: linter score improves or remains within tolerance, compile_rate should be 100%, no change in behavior.

Dataset curation notes (how prompts/examples are created):
- Source of seeds: internal sample repos, anonymized community snippets, and curated micro-benchmarks that exercise edge cases (concurrency, numeric precision, null handling).
- Each prompt comes with a small reference harness repo that includes golden tests, a small README, and the compile/test container definition.
- Prompts are intentionally short to force the model to supply runnable code; long multi-file scaffolds are covered in a separate integration suite.

Safety and guardrails:
- System prompts include explicit rules: no external network calls, no reading secrets, no making system calls outside the sandbox.
- Outputs are scanned for suspicious patterns (calls to os.system, exec, network libs). Any such outputs are quarantined and marked manual-review.

Representative regression report (summary of a candidate run vs baseline - fictional numbers to illustrate format):
- baseline_model: code-v2.3
- candidate_model: code-v3-experimental
- run_date: 2026-02-25
- corpus_size: 120 prompts (30 per taxonomy category)
- compile_rate: baseline=0.81, candidate=0.88 (+7pp)
- test_pass_rate: baseline=0.74, candidate=0.70 (-4pp) => flagged: drop in test_pass_rate despite higher compile_rate; requires triage.
- behavior_preservation (surgery): baseline=0.92, candidate=0.86 (-6pp) => moderate regression on refactors that preserve nuanced edge behaviors (race conditions emulated in tests).
- style_violation_rate: baseline=0.22, candidate=0.08 (improvement)
- notes: candidate generates more compact patches and fewer linter violations but introduced subtle semantic regressions in concurrent list mutation tests. Suspected cause: more aggressive transformations that remove locks in refactor outputs.
- action items: block promotion to dedicated catalog, run focused concurrency prompt suite (see linked artifact RL-1304), add 5 targeted few-shot examples that demonstrate preserving locks, re-run.

Checklist for onboarding a new model (quick gate):
- [ ] Run full prompt suite (all temps) on 120 prompt corpus.
- [ ] Compile rate >= baseline -5pp OR test_pass_rate >= baseline -3pp.
- [ ] No rule-violating outputs (security) in >1% of runs.
- [ ] Linter regressions <= baseline + 5pp.
- [ ] Manual review signoff for surgery prompts where behavior_preservation < 90%.

Open questions / TODOs (working items):
- Expand Java/C++ surgery prompts for ABI surface testing.
- Define a deterministic metric for 'intent drift' beyond unit tests (semantic similarity tooling).
- Create a small human-in-the-loop UI for rapid triage of flagged refactors.
- Collect more examples where minimal patch (1-5 lines) is expected and verify model shrinkage behavior.

Appendix: quick example entries from the prompt bank (representative, not exhaustive):
- pb-001: python-synthesis-sort-key-stable-2026 — stable-sort implementation focusing on key functions and in-place requirements.
- pb-043: js-surgery-flatten-edgecase — fixes for nested flattening logic including non-array inputs.
- pb-077: go-style-naming-exported-comments — small refactors for exported function docs and naming.

If you use this doc, please link run artifacts back into `linked_artifacts`. Use the PR referenced above for updating the harness runner. This doc is intentionally informal: add concrete failures and test snippets as you triage so the next reviewer sees concrete repros.
